critical_steps: The sequence Lambda_n x=x_n/n is g-Bessel and has synthesis T=diag(1/n).
The vector (1/n^2) lies in R(T*) but not in R(T*T).
R(T*T) is always contained in R(T*).
Douglas factorization shows the reverse inclusion forces a spectral gap for T*T and hence closed range.
Closed range conversely gives the reverse inclusion by orthogonal decomposition.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact diagonal synthesis operator on l2 and Douglas range inclusion.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made that downstream results with independent closed-range hypotheses fail.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects the discrete Lemma 2.1 and continuous Lemma 2.4, not every downstream theorem in the two papers.
The closed-range equivalence is standard operator theory; the new claim is the source-specific correction and explicit g-Bessel witness.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: A closed-range boundary for Gram-range inclusion in \(g\)-Bessel sequences
